drivers.explain: If a dispute arises, the person who decides it is chosen by the other side alone. The forum that judges the quarrel is picked by one of the parties to it.

statute.section: Section 28(b), read with section 28(a) — Agreements in restraint of legal proceedings, void
statute.text: Every agreement, (a) by which any party thereto is restricted absolutely from enforcing his rights under or in respect of any contract, by the usual legal proceedings in the ordinary tribunals, or which limits the time within which he may thus enforce his rights; or (b) which extinguishes the rights of any party thereto, or discharges any party thereto from any liability, under or in respect of any contract on the expiry of a specified period so as to restrict any party from enforcing his rights, is void to that extent.

enforceability.plainMeaning: A clause that gives you only thirty or ninety days to raise a claim, or that says your rights disappear after a short period, does not usually take away the time the general law of limitation gives you.
caveats: This describes the section, not your contract. Whether a particular clause falls inside it is for a court to decide.
Clause (b) was added by the 1997 amendment; decisions from before 1997 that upheld clauses extinguishing rights on expiry pre-date that change.
The section does not extend the time the Limitation Act gives you. That clock runs from when your cause of action arose, whatever the contract says.
Arbitration clauses that set a period for commencing arbitration are treated separately and are not all caught by this section.

statute.section: Section 27 — Agreement in restraint of trade, void
statute.text: Every agreement by which any one is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business of any kind, is to that extent void.

authorities.cite: Niranjan Shankar Golikari v The Century Spinning and Mfg Co Ltd, AIR 1967 SC 1098 (17 January 1967)
authorities.holding: A restraint that operates while the employment is still running was upheld; the Supreme Court treated restrictions that bite after the employment ends as standing on a different footing under section 27.

authorities.cite: Varun Tyagi v Daffodil Software Private Limited, FAO 167/2025, Delhi High Court (25 June 2025)
authorities.holding: A clause barring the employee from working with a business associate of the employer after the employment ended was held void under section 27; confidentiality and trade-secret protection was treated as the legitimate route instead.

enforceability.plainMeaning: Indian law generally does not enforce a promise not to work for a competitor after your job ends. India has no test of reasonableness that saves such a promise, unlike England or the United States. The confidentiality promise sitting next to it is a separate thing and usually does still hold.
caveats: This describes what the section says and how courts have read it. It is not an opinion about your contract or your situation.
A restraint that applies while you are still employed is treated differently and is often enforced.
Protection of trade secrets, client data and confidential information can bind you after you leave, even when the non-compete does not.
The other side can still sue. Only a court can decide what this clause does on your facts, and defending a suit costs time and money.
Garden leave, notice buy-outs and non-solicitation clauses raise separate questions this row does not cover.

statute.section: Section 12(5), read with the Seventh Schedule
statute.text: Notwithstanding any prior agreement to the contrary, any person whose relationship, with the parties or counsel or the subject-matter of the dispute, falls under any of the categories specified in the Seventh Schedule shall be ineligible to be appointed as an arbitrator: Provided that parties may, subsequent to disputes having arisen between them, waive the applicability of this sub-section by an express agreement in writing.

authorities.cite: Perkins Eastman Architects DPC v HSCC (India) Ltd, Arbitration Application No. 32 of 2019, Supreme Court (26 November 2019)
authorities.holding: A person who has an interest in the outcome of the dispute must not have the power to appoint a sole arbitrator; where the clause gave one party's managing director that power, the Court appointed an independent arbitrator instead.

authorities.cite: The Seventh Schedule to the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (See section 12(5))
authorities.holding: Lists the relationships — employee, consultant, adviser, controlling interest and others — that make a person ineligible to act as arbitrator.

enforceability.plainMeaning: When only one side gets to choose the arbitrator, courts have held that the person chosen cannot decide the dispute. The agreement to arbitrate usually survives; it is the one-sided appointment that does not.
caveats: This states what the section and the Supreme Court have held. It is not an opinion on the clause in your document.
The parties can waive this by an express written agreement made after a dispute has arisen, so signing anything at that stage deserves care.
Setting an appointment aside is done by applying to a court, usually under section 11; the clause does not simply stop working on its own.
Clauses where one side supplies a panel from which the other must choose have been treated in later decisions and are not decided by this row.
Government and public-sector contracts have their own line of cases on departmental arbitrators.

statute.section: Section 23 — What considerations and objects are lawful, and what not
statute.text: The consideration or object of an agreement is lawful, unless it is forbidden by law; or is of such a nature that, if permitted, it would defeat the provisions of any law; or is fraudulent; or involves or implies injury to the person or property of another; or the Court regards it as immoral, or opposed to public policy. In each of these cases, the consideration or object of an agreement is said to be unlawful. Every agreement of which the object or consideration is unlawful is void.

authorities.cite: Central Inland Water Transport Corporation Ltd v Brojo Nath Ganguly, (1986) 3 SCC 156 (6 April 1986)
authorities.holding: A term in a printed standard-form contract between parties of unequal bargaining power, which is unfair, unreasonable and unconscionable, was held void under section 23 as opposed to public policy.

enforceability.plainMeaning: Courts have struck down terms in standard printed contracts where one side had no real chance to negotiate and the term was grossly one-sided. Whether a particular term is of that kind depends on the bargaining position of the two sides.
caveats: This is the general principle, not a ruling on your clause. Only a court applying it to your facts can say whether the term stands.
Brojo Nath concerned an instrumentality of the State; later decisions have been cautious about extending it to contracts between commercial parties of comparable strength.
Showing unequal bargaining power is part of the case and has to be proved, not assumed.
A consumer complaint about an unfair contract term may be a quicker route than a civil suit; the routes are separate.

forum.name: Conciliation Officer or Labour Commissioner, then the Labour Court
forum.handles: Unpaid or delayed wages, illegal termination, retrenchment, gratuity and provident fund.
forum.statute: Code on Wages, 2019, s.17; Industrial Relations Code, 2020; Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, s.2A

portal.name: SAMADHAN, the Ministry of Labour and Employment's dispute portal

fee.summary: Free. Raising a dispute and the conciliation that follows cost nothing.

forum.filingPlace: With the Conciliation Officer or Labour Commissioner having jurisdiction over the establishment. SAMADHAN routes the complaint to the right office.

prerequisites.step: Raise the dispute before the Conciliation Officer first. s.2A(2) allows a direct application to the Labour Court only after this.
Provident fund grievances go to EPFiGMS instead, which is run by the EPFO and answers separately.

entitlements: Code on Wages, 2019, s.17(2) — where an employee is removed, dismissed, retrenched or resigns, the wages payable must be paid within two working days.

Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, s.25F — retrenchment without one month's notice or notice pay, and without retrenchment compensation, is invalid. The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 carries the same conditions forward.
caveats: The four Labour Codes were brought into force on 21 November 2025 and the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 no longer stands on its own. Rights that had accrued and proceedings already begun are saved, and the corresponding provision of the Industrial Relations Code, 2020 governs a termination after that date — confirm which applies to your dates before relying on the period shown.
State rules under the Codes have been notified unevenly, so what the office in front of you follows may still be the older procedure.

The conciliation route is open to a workman as defined in s.2(s) of the 1947 Act and the corresponding definition in the Code. Mainly supervisory or managerial work above the wage threshold falls outside it.
Gratuity is claimed separately, from the Controlling Authority.

limitationRule.causeOfAction: The date of discharge, dismissal, retrenchment or other termination of service.

stages.label: Wait after applying to the Conciliation Officer before going to the Labour Court
stages.from: the date the application for conciliation is made

forum.name: District or State Legal Services Authority
forum.handles: Free legal advice, drafting and representation by a panel advocate for anyone within s.12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
forum.statute: Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, ss.12 and 13

fee.summary: Free, including court fees, process fees and the panel advocate, for anyone eligible under s.12.

forum.filingPlace: At the District Legal Services Authority in your district court complex, which accepts walk-in applications, or online through the NALSA portal.
entitlements: s.12(c) and s.12(f) entitle every woman, every child and every industrial workman to free legal services irrespective of what they earn.
s.12(h) entitles a person whose annual income is below the ceiling their State has fixed, and Rs 5,00,000 applies to Supreme Court matters.
Tele-Law connects you to a panel lawyer free of charge through a Common Service Centre or the Tele-Law app (tele-law.in), which is offered in 22 languages.
caveats: Eligibility is decided by the Authority on the application and the documents filed with it.
Applying for free legal aid does not stop the limitation period for the underlying claim from running.

forum.name: Lok Adalat
forum.handles: Settlement by consent of a pending case or of a dispute before any case is filed, organised by the Legal Services Authority.
forum.statute: Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, ss.19 to 22B

fee.summary: Free, and s.21 refunds the court fee already paid when a pending case is settled.

forum.filingPlace: Through the District Legal Services Authority, which publishes the dates of the National Lok Adalat held each quarter.
entitlements: s.21 — an award of a Lok Adalat is deemed to be a decree of a civil court, is final, and no appeal lies against it.
s.21(1) proviso — the court fee paid in a pending case is refunded when the matter is settled in a Lok Adalat.
s.22B — a Permanent Lok Adalat hears public utility service disputes up to Rs 1,00,00,000 and may decide the matter on merits if no settlement is reached.
caveats: A Lok Adalat records a settlement both sides agree to. Apart from a Permanent Lok Adalat under s.22C, it decides nothing by itself.
Because an award is final and no appeal lies from it, what is agreed there cannot later be reopened.
Waiting for a Lok Adalat date does not stop the limitation period for filing from running.
